titulo: How to help keep your pipes from freezing
receta: error cotidiano + regla para guardar (qué hacer la noche que baja de cero)
destinatario: Se lo manda alguien a su amigo o a su papá que se olvida de todo hasta que la cañería ya se rompió.

interaccion.guardar: Freezing night: drip the faucet, open the cabinet doors under the sinks, keep the heat on (no lower than 55°F).
interaccion.comentar: Do you drip your faucets when it freezes? Yes or no?

fuentes: FEMA: 5 Ways to Safely Weather the Storm (fema.gov/blog/5-ways-safely-weather-storm)
National Weather Service New York: weather.gov/okx/winterpns7 and weather.gov/okx/extremecoldpns

frases.texto: On a freezing night, the water in your pipes can freeze.
Here's one simple step: let a faucet drip.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: FEMA says a slow drip keeps water moving through the pipes, which reduces the chance of freezing.
The National Weather Service adds two more: open the cabinet doors under your sinks, so warmer air can reach the pipes.
And keep the heat on, no lower than fifty-five degrees.
Heads up: this lowers the chance of freezing. It's not a guarantee.
Save this for the next freezing night: drip the faucet, open the cabinets, keep the heat on.
Do you drip your faucets when it freezes? Yes or no?
Send this to the friend who finds out about the pipes in the morning.
